name: Multi-timeframe DIVERGENCE pullback — slow uptrend, fast band-washout (long spot)
rationale: MULTI-TIMEFRAME DIVERGENCE (not confirmation). dual-timeframe-momentum-confirmation requires fast AND slow momentum to AGREE (both up). This spec deliberately requires them to DISAGREE in the buy-the-dip way: a SLOW lookback return solidly positive (the higher-timeframe trend is intact) WHILE the FAST, statistically-measured price is washed out below its band (a short-term dislocation against the trend) — the textbook 'pullback within an uptrend' but read on two distinct timescales with two distinct feature types (slow ret_Nd for trend, bb_z for the fast statistical washout, so the two series never collide on a shared lookback). Mechanism before data: long spot when ret_Nd over a slow window is above a trend floor AND bb_z is below a fitted washout floor (price stretched below its mean) AND realized vol contained; exit when bb_z normalizes back toward the mean (dip resolved) or barriers fire. Distinct from rsi-dip-buy-in-an-uptrend (rsi dip + ret trend + vol — uses RSI not bb_z, and not framed as cross-timescale divergence) and bollinger-z-score-washout-reversion (washout + vol, NO higher-timeframe trend arm — it buys washouts in any regime). The novelty is the explicit slow-trend-UP x fast-washout-DOWN divergence. Disconfirmer 1: drop the slow trend arm — if a bare bb_z washout matches the deflated Sharpe, the higher-timeframe filter adds nothing and this is the existing washout spec. Disconfirmer 2: drop the bb_z arm — if slow-trend-long alone matches, it is just trend-following. Disconfirmer 3 (PIT/cost): both computed at bar close; net of ~20bps the pullback bounce must clear. tier0 ret_Nd + tier0 bb_z/vol, computed-at-backtest, unproven combination — low-confidence until OOS.
catalyst: a positive SLOW-timeframe trend WHILE the FAST statistical price (bb_z) is washed out below its band — a higher-timeframe pullback, bought on spot
